fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions of approach.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the front driveway to maintain clear vehicle passage from the road to the parking area.
• Mark or number both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can immediately identify which building is being referenced during an emergency.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure free of parked vehicles, equipment, or stored materials.
• Trim vegetation along the sides of the driveway to allow a full-size emergency vehicle to reach the parking area without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation along any pathway that connects the rear of the property to the front, so responders can move between structures on foot.
• Keep the rear of the detached structure accessible on foot by maintaining a clear gap between the structure and surrounding vegetation.
• If a gate controls access to the rear of the property, keep it unlocked or install a knox-box so responders can reach the back of the lot without delay.
• Identify and maintain at least one clear, unobstructed walking route around each structure so responders can circle the building during an emergency.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees that hang over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create gaps between their canopies.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from the base of trees to reduce the connection between low plants and tree canopies.
• Keep the area beneath large trees clear of dead leaves, branches, and low-growing plants.
• Thin scattered trees on the approach side of the structure to maintain open sightlines and movement around the building.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along their edges.
